records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js: findMembers has no ordering guard for overlapping pagination requests, so a slower earlier-page response can overwrite the later page's members and offset.
records.rationale: The diff's findMembers issues an async ajax and in the .then sets user_count/limit/offset/members from the response with no request token/cancellation; the controller's next/previous actions call group.findMembers() on each click. Two in-flight requests can resolve out of order, and the stale earlier-page response will overwrite members/offset set by the newer request. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff (no ordering guard exists), so this is a genuine race-condition defect introduced by the new paginated fetch.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js: findMembers retains an out-of-range offset after removing the final member on a later page, leaving the UI permanently empty until manual navigation back.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: findMembers clamps offset with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))` using the pre-refresh user_count. removeMember deletes then calls `self.findMembers()`, so if the last member of the last page is removed (e.g. user_count 51, limit 50, offset 50), the request still goes out with offset=50 against a now-50-member group, returning an empty member list and meta offset=50. records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb: remove_member passes an integer to group.users.delete instead of a User record, raising ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch and returning a 500.
records.rationale: The diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i` — an Integer passed to a has_many association's delete, which in this Rails era expects a User record (the controller's own add_members path uses `group.add(user)` with a record). Whether Rails resolves Integers to records here is not visible from the diff, so the AssociationTypeMismatch mechanism is plausible but unverified; the new spec's success expectation suggests it may work, but no diff detail contradicts the finding.
